EVERY PHOTO LOADED — check the order before you run

widgets_values:
You are a senior real-estate video producer writing the shot plan for a property walkthrough.

You will receive a set of photographs of one property, in the order they should appear in the film, and the number of slots to fill.

COUNT THE PHOTOGRAPHS FIRST, and output exactly that many objects — one per photograph, in the order given. No more and no fewer. Do not pad the list to a round number: the
only correct length is the number of photographs in front of you. Never merge two photographs into one shot, never skip a photograph because it resembles an earlier one, never stop early, and never summarise a long set. A short plan is not a shorter film: the photographs past the end of your plan are still rendered, and they all reuse the LAST line you wrote, so the film ends with the same sentence repeated over different rooms. If a room appears several times, write a different line for each appearance.

For EACH photograph, in order, decide:
- scene: its position, counting from 1.
- room: which part of the property it shows. One of Exterior, Entrance, Living Room, Kitchen, Bedroom, Bathroom, Dining Room, Office, Garden, Other.
- video_prompt: one sentence of camera direction for an image-to-video model. Describe a SINGLE slow, continuous move that suits the room — a gentle push in, a slow pan across, a soft tilt up to the ceiling, a drift towards a window. Say what the camera does, not what the room contains. Never invent objects, never change the architecture, and never cut.
- voiceText: what the agent says over that shot. Warm and factual, selling the feeling of the space. Do not read out a feature list, and never mention price.

  **Every shot runs exactly 12.25 seconds, and the last 4.0 seconds of it must be SILENT.** The picture keeps moving while nobody speaks — that pause is what lets one room settle before the next arrives, and a film without it is a wall of talking. So you are writing for 8.0 seconds of speech, not 12.25.

  That means between 15 and 19 words, and NEVER more than 19 words. This is a hard limit, not a style note. The voice can read as slowly as 2.4 words a second, so 19 words already fills the whole speaking window; anything longer eats the pause. The picture cannot be stretched to cover a longer line — it would hold a frozen frame instead.

  Short is safe here. A line that ends early simply gives a longer, calmer beat.
- seconds: how long the shot should run. Ignored — the shot length is decided by the workflow, not by this plan. Fill it in anyway so the JSON shape stays constant.

Write the FIRST shot as an arrival and the LAST as a close. Keep one voice throughout, as though the same person walks you round the whole property.

Output ONLY a JSON array, one object per photograph, with exactly these keys: scene, room, video_prompt, voiceText, seconds.

The key is voiceText, spelled exactly like that — camelCase, no underscore. The node that reads this plan looks for that spelling and silently produces nothing for any other.

No preamble, no markdown, no commentary.

widgets_values:
# ▶ START HERE — Property Walkthrough AI

Point this at a folder of property photographs and it writes a shot plan, speaks the
narration in a voice you supply, animates every photo with **LTX-2.5**, and joins the
whole thing into one narrated walkthrough film with subtitles.

**Any number of photos.** Thirty listing photographs render as thirty shots.

*Workflow by **Hisham**.  Custom nodes: https://github.com/Hishamahmer/comfyui-arkennemasis*

## Will it run on my computer?

| | |
|---|---|
| Models | **37 GB** on disk, plus room for the film |
| Measured | RTX A6000, 48 GB — **9 photographs to a finished 1 min 31 s film in 20 min 58 s** |
| Per shot | about **2 min 12 s**, steady. The first is ~25 s longer because the models load |
| Headroom | at this size a 48 GB card had to push about 1.8 GB of the model back out to make room. A smaller card will not hold it |

Where the 21 minutes went, measured on that run:

| stage | time |
|---|---|
| Writing the shot plan (all 9 photographs, one call) | **27 s** |
| Speaking each line | **20-25 s** a shot, for 5-7 s of speech |
| Rendering each shot | **about 2 min** — this is almost the whole cost |
| Joining, subtitles, levelling | **14 s** for the lot |

**The render is ~95% of the time, and it scales with the number of photographs, not with
anything else.** Nine photographs is about twenty minutes; thirty is about an hour.

The finished file: 1280x704, 24 fps, h264 with AAC audio. It comes out 704 rather than the
736 the box asks for — the model rounds the height down to a size it can work in. That is
normal and nothing to fix.

**On a smaller card, drop the frame size before anything else.** Open the
`LTX-2.5 — image to video` box and lower `width` and `height` — keep both multiples of
32. 960x544 and 768x448 both work and cost far less memory. Resolution is the setting
that decides whether this fits, and it is the first thing to change.

## 1 · Install five node packs

Open a terminal in your ComfyUI folder and run these five lines. Then **close ComfyUI and
start it again** — new packs are only picked up at startup.

```
cd ComfyUI\custom_nodes
git clone https://github.com/Hishamahmer/comfyui-arkennemasis
git clone https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-KJNodes
git clone https://github.com/yolain/ComfyUI-Easy-Use
git clone https://github.com/pythongosssss/ComfyUI-Custom-Scripts
git clone https://github.com/rgthree/rgthree-comfy
```

| pack | what it gives this workflow |
|---|---|
| `ComfyUI-KJNodes` | the photo-folder loader, and the Set/Get shortcuts |
| `ComfyUI-Easy-Use` | the loop that renders one shot at a time |
| `ComfyUI-Custom-Scripts` | the boxes that show you the shot plan |
| `rgthree-comfy` | the box that takes whichever writer you left enabled |
| **`comfyui-arkennemasis`** | **every node whose name starts with `Ark`, and the shot-plan box. This is the workflow's own pack — https://github.com/Hishamahmer/comfyui-arkennemasis** |

If a pack has a `requirements.txt`, install it with ComfyUI's own Python, never a system
one, and pin the big packages first so nothing replaces your CUDA build of PyTorch:

```
python_embeded\python.exe -m pip freeze | findstr /B /I "torch torchvision torchaudio numpy pillow transformers" > %TEMP%\pins.txt
set PIP_CONSTRAINT=%TEMP%\pins.txt
python_embeded\python.exe -m pip install -r ComfyUI\custom_nodes\<pack>\requirements.txt
```

**Never run `pip install -r ComfyUI\requirements.txt --upgrade`.** `torch` is unpinned in
that file, so `--upgrade` quietly swaps your CUDA build for a CPU-only one. Nothing
renders afterwards and the cause is invisible.

## 2 · Download five models

**Read this first.** The official repository, https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5 ,
is **gated**: you must open that page, sign in and accept the licence, and then download
while logged in. Without that every link below returns an error instead of a file.

| save it in | file | size |
|---|---|---|
| `ComfyUI\models\diffusion_models\` | `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors` | 20.0 GB |
| `ComfyUI\models\text_encoders\` | `gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors` | 14.3 GB |
| `ComfyUI\models\vae\` | `ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors` | 1.37 GB |
| `ComfyUI\models\vae\` | `ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors` | 0.34 GB |
| `ComfyUI\models\latent_upscale_models\` | `ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors` | 0.93 GB |

```
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/vae/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/resolve/main/latent_upscale_models/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors
```

**If you would rather not sign the licence**, three of the five are mirrored openly and
are the same files, byte for byte:

```
https://huggingface.co/ChrisColeTech/LTX-2.5-turbo-GGUF/resolve/main/split/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/ChrisColeTech/LTX-2.5-turbo-GGUF/resolve/main/split/vae/ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors
https://huggingface.co/ChrisColeTech/LTX-2.5-turbo-GGUF/resolve/main/split/latent_upscale_models/ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors
```

The transformer and the text encoder have no open mirror in a form this workflow can
load, so those two do need the licence. It takes a minute and costs nothing.

**The names must match exactly.** These boxes remember a filename; a different one shows
the node in red and it will not run.

## 3 · Nothing else to install for the picture

All five files load with ComfyUI's built-in loaders. There is no extra pack to install
for the video model.

## 4 · The voice — one-off setup

The narration is spoken locally by Qwen3-TTS. Download both folders into
`ComfyUI\models\qwen-tts\`, keeping the folder names exactly as they are:

| folder | size | where from |
|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base` | 2.52 GB | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-Base |
| `Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz` | 0.68 GB | https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz |

Then create the voice engine's own private copy of one library. This does **not** touch
your main install — it installs into a folder of its own:

```
python_embeded\python.exe -m pip install -t ComfyUI\custom_nodes\comfyui-arkennemasis\vendor --no-deps qwen-tts==0.1.1
python_embeded\python.exe -m pip install -t ComfyUI\custom_nodes\comfyui-arkennemasis\vendor\tts_env --no-deps "transformers==4.57.3" "huggingface-hub>=0.34.0,<1.0" "tokenizers>=0.22.0,<=0.23.0"
```

**Both lines, and in that order.** The first puts the speech engine itself in
`vendor\qwen_tts`; the second puts the one library it disagrees with the rest of ComfyUI
about in `vendor\tts_env`. That `vendor` folder is not part of the download — it is built
here, on your machine — so a fresh copy of the pack has neither until you run these.

Do **not** fix this by downgrading `transformers` everywhere. Eleven other packs need the
newer one; that is the whole reason this lives in its own folder.

## 5 · The story engine — pick one of two

The **LLM** box holds two writers and a switch between them. Only the one you pick ever
runs, so the other costs nothing at all — nothing to download, nothing to log into, no
time spent.

### Which one should I use?

| | **OpenAI** | **Local Gemma 3** |
|---|---|---|
| VRAM while it writes | **none** — it runs on someone else's computer | **18.7 GB** measured, at the shipped `n_ctx` |
| Download | nothing | **7.6 GB** (the model, plus the part that lets it see) |
| Needs | a ChatGPT / Codex login, and internet | nothing — it works offline |
| Cost per run | one call on your account | nothing |
| Speed | about **27 s** for nine photographs | a few seconds, plus loading the model the first time |
| Writing quality | better, noticeably | good enough, and it obeys the length rule less reliably |

**On a card under 20 GB, use OpenAI.** It asks nothing of your graphics card at all, so
the whole VRAM budget stays with the renderer where it matters.

**If you want the local model on a smaller card**, two widgets on the
**Local Gemma 3** node control the bill. Turn on `advanced` to see them:

| `n_ctx` | VRAM | holds |
|---|---|---|
| 8192 | **15.6 GB** | roughly 20 photographs |
| 16384 | **18.7 GB** | roughly 30 photographs — the shipped value |
| 32768 | **25.2 GB** | more than you need, and a lot more memory |

Measured on a 48 GB card idling at 3.4 GB. The numbers are this large because Gemma 3
keeps a full-size attention cache — the 6.8 GB of weights is the small half of the bill.
Each photograph costs about 256 tokens of context, so lower `n_ctx` only as far as your
photograph count allows.

Still too big? Lower `n_gpu_layers` from 99. Each step moves part of the model to
ordinary RAM: slower to write, but it fits. It only has to do this once per run.

**Either way the writer is gone before the renderer starts** — `unload_after_run` is on,
so nothing it used is still held when LTX begins staging its 20 GB.

### Switching between them — one action

The two writers sit in boxes of their own on the canvas:

- **2A · OPENAI · ENABLED**
- **2B · LOCAL GEMMA 3 · DISABLED**

**Right-click the box you want and choose Set Group Nodes to Always (on) or Never (off).**
Turn one on, turn the other off. That is the whole switch — there is no separate tickbox
to keep in step with it.

A disabled writer is not merely skipped, it is **gone from the run**: its models are never
loaded and never even checked. So the OpenAI side runs on a machine with no Gemma files on
disk, and the local side runs with no ChatGPT login. Download only the one you plan to use.

**Leave exactly one enabled.** With both off there is no plan at all; with both on you get
whichever the merge box happens to read last.

### ON — OpenAI

Signs in with an existing **ChatGPT / Codex login** rather than an API key. Install the
Codex CLI from https://github.com/openai/codex and run `codex login` once. It saves
`auth.json` in `%USERPROFILE%\.codex`, which is where the node looks. Better writing,
and it needs an account.

### OFF — local Gemma 3, free and offline

No account, no internet, no per-run cost. Download two files into
`ComfyUI\models\LLM\gemma-3-12b\` from
https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-3-12b-it-GGUF :

| file | size |
|---|---|
| `gemma-3-12b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` | 6.8 GB |
| `mmproj-F16.gguf` | 0.82 GB |

The second one is the part that lets it SEE the photographs; without it you get a plan
written blind. This writer also needs one more pack —
https://github.com/vrgamegirl19/comfyui-vrgamedevgirl — and about 8 GB of VRAM while
it works. It unloads itself as soon as it is done, so it does not compete with the
renderer that runs next.

**Use Gemma 3, not Gemma 4.** A Gemma 4 file will load and answer, and the answer will be
nonsense rather than an error — so the plan reads as badly written rather than obviously
broken. The boxes are already set to the right file.

## 6 · Your photos and your voice sample

- Put the property photos in **one folder**, named so they sort in the order you want them
  to appear — `01-front.jpg`, `02-hall.jpg`, and so on. Type that folder's path into
  **THE PROPERTY PHOTOS** at the far left.
- **Any number of photos works.** 30 listing photos render as 30 shots. The loader has no
  cap, and the loop renders one shot at a time and frees it before the next, so 30 photos
  cost the same memory as 3 — only time.
- For the narrator's voice, drop a clean recording of one person talking — **under 20
  seconds**, `.mp3` or `.wav` — into `ComfyUI\input\` and pick it on the voice node. Skip
  this and you get the model's stock voice instead.

Keep the sample short. The cloner listens to the whole clip **once per shot**, so a long
sample multiplies across every shot in the film. An 81-second sample once left a single
shot still going after eight minutes.

## 7 · Press Run — then check two numbers

Before anything expensive happens, two small boxes tell you whether the plan is sound:

- **HOW MANY PHOTOS** — how many pictures were found in your folder.
- **HOW MANY SHOTS THE PLAN WROTE** — how many shots the story agent planned.

**These two numbers must match.** They are the cheapest check in the whole workflow and
they catch the two things that actually go wrong:

- **Fewer shots than photos** — the extra photographs still render, but they all reuse the
  final narration line, and you find out twenty minutes later while watching the film.
- **More shots than photos** — the writer padded the list. Nothing warns you; the plan
  simply describes rooms that were never photographed.

If they disagree, run the plan again. It takes under half a minute and costs nothing worth
counting; the render costs twenty.

Read **THE SHOT PLAN** box too. Fixing a bad plan is free. Rendering one is not.

### What a finished run looks like

From a real run of nine photographs:

```
scene list: 9 scenes, lengths [243 x 9] frames (10.1 s each)
run folder: ...\shots\ltx
un_002
scene 1/9 ... scene 9/9
assembling 9 clips (90.4s total), speech normalised to -16 LUFS
9 subtitle cues from the scene plan
final video -> walkthrough_ltx.mp4 (46.5 MB)
Prompt executed in 00:20:58
```

Nine shots for nine photographs, every shot the same 10.1 s, one subtitle cue each. Each
run gets its own numbered folder, so a second run never mixes with the first and an
interrupted one keeps everything it had already finished.

## 8 · Captions

**CAPTIONS — ON / OFF** sits next to the node that joins the film. Tick it for burned-in
subtitles, untick it for a clean picture. Nothing else changes.

## Where the film lands

`ComfyUI\output\realestate\video-workflows\property-walkthrough\`

Each shot is written into its own numbered `run_XXX` folder as it finishes, so an
interrupted run keeps everything it already rendered and nothing is ever overwritten.

## If it goes wrong

| what you see | what it means |
|---|---|
| A loader box is red | The filename on disk is not exactly the one in section 2. Rename it. |
| Downloads fail with 401 or "access denied" | You have not accepted the licence on the Lightricks page, or you are not signed in. See section 2. |
| `mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied` | Wrong text encoder. It must be the LTX-2.5 one named in section 2. |
| The film is silent | The **audio** VAE is missing. It is a separate file from the video VAE. |
| Out of memory | Lower `width` and `height` on the `LTX-2.5 — image to video` box, in steps of 32. See the table at the top. |
| `text is empty` on the voice node | The shot plan came back in the wrong shape. Look at THE SHOT PLAN box and run the plan again. |
| The last few shots all say the same line | The plan was shorter than your photo count. See section 7. |
| The log freezes right after startup | You pressed Run before ComfyUI finished loading. Wait for the console to settle and try again. |

## How the canvas is laid out

Three boxes:

- **YOUR PHOTOS** — the folder you point at, and a preview of what was found.
- **LLM OPENAI** — the brief, and the model that turns your photographs into a shot plan.
  It runs once per press, however many photographs you give it.
- **THE FILM** — the loop that renders each shot, speaks its line, and joins the result.

The first two feed the third through named shortcuts rather than long wires, which is why
no cable runs the width of the canvas.

---

# Setting this up with an AI agent

If you would rather not do the above by hand, select **everything from this line to the
end of the note**, copy it, and give it to an agent with a terminal on this machine
(Claude Code, Codex, or similar).

---

You are setting up one ComfyUI workflow — **Property Walkthrough AI, the LTX-2.5 lane** — on
this Windows machine. ComfyUI portable is already installed and starts. Work through the
sections above this line, in order, and verify each step on disk before moving on.

Ground rules:

- Use `python_embeded\python.exe` for every pip command. Never a system Python.
- Never run `pip install -r ComfyUI\requirements.txt --upgrade`. Set `PIP_CONSTRAINT` as
  shown before installing any node dependencies.
- Restart ComfyUI after installing custom nodes, before opening the workflow.
- Model filenames must match the tables exactly. Verify each file's size on disk against
  the size in the table — a truncated download looks like a present file.
- Freshly downloaded binaries are sometimes blocked by Windows Application Control. If an
  import fails with "An Application Control policy has blocked this file", relaunch
  first; if it persists, run
  `Get-ChildItem <site-packages> -Recurse -Include *.dll,*.pyd | Unblock-File`.

When you are finished, do not report success from a clean log. Verify honestly:

1. A film exists under `ComfyUI\output\realestate\video-workflows\property-walkthrough\`
   and is more than a megabyte.
2. `ffprobe` reports an `h264` video stream and an `aac` audio stream.
3. Its duration is roughly 10 seconds per photograph supplied.
4. Open it. It shows the property, and you can hear the narration.

Report what you did, what you verified, and anything you could not.

widgets_values: Egyptian royal in blue-and-gold headdress and high collar, white dress with golden embroidery and armbands, desert, robot soldiers in formation left and right. She walks steadily forward, head held level and gaze fixed ahead—no dipping or lowering of the head. The camera performs a single, smooth push-in only: starting in a wider shot of her, the robots, and the desert, it moves steadily forward until she is in a medium or medium-close frame, then holds. She stops, posture and head still upright, and says: “The old gods are silent. I am not.” Robot soldiers shift or march in place; sand and fabric move with the wind. No pull-back; the only camera move is the continuous push-in.
